provider: RepOD — Repository for Open Data (ICM, University of Warsaw)

free_tier.stated: No dataset-size limit at all: 'Repozytorium akceptuje zbiory danych o dowolnej wielkości. Jedynym ograniczeniem jest limit wielkości pojedynczego pliku, wynoszący 5GB' (the repository accepts datasets of any size; the only limit is 5 GB per single file). A sibling UW deposit guide adds '20 GB for the sum of files transferred simultaneously'. Storage itself is unpriced: 'Korzystanie z repozytorium nie wiąże się z żadnymi opłatami' (using the repository involves no fees).

retention.stated: Publication assigns a DOI and freezes that version — versions are immutable after publish, so this is write-once-per-version, not mutable working storage

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. Public files are plain HTTP from repod.icm.edu.pl with no egress pricing anywhere in the product; downloads are the same Dataverse /api/access/datafile path used by Harvard. Probe: GET /api/access/datafile/39782 -> 200, 7,459 bytes returned, MD5 published per file for verification.

tooling: Native Dataverse 4.11 REST API, live and unauthenticated for reads: GET /api/info/version -> {"version":"1.3.2-05b9a3acf7fe552a849e874762b86d0605e47186"}; GET /api/search?q=*&type=dataset -> total_count 4545; type=file -> 65370 items. The repository's own policy page states uploads work 'zarowno przez graficzny interfejs ... jak i za pomocą interfejsu API' (both GUI and API). Standard Dataverse ingest: DVUploader (github.com/GlobalDataverseCommunityConsortium/dataverse-uploader), pyDataverse, SWORD v2. No rclone backend, but the REST loop is ~15 lines.
chaining: Per-record cap is the unit, not per-account: unlimited datasets x unlimited size each, so 500 GB is 100 files of 5 GB inside one dataset — no account multiplication needed. Multiple datasets multiply further. One email/password account is enough; signup is self-service ('Sign up for an account to log in with your email or username and password').
limits_note: Per-object-cap 5 GB/file and 20 GB per simultaneous transfer batch are the only hard numbers; there is NO per-dataset and NO per-account byte ceiling. 1,000 files per zip ingest (Dataverse default). Publication assigns a DOI and freezes that version — versions are immutable after publish, so this is write-once-per-version, not mutable working storage. Embargo up to 36 months.
